analysis:
Examined all three primary analyses and the replayed action, workflow and documentation patches. The analyses are not independent proof; replay is incomplete (11 source units omitted), including the ci.yml enforcement source.

.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml:7–9 makes cache saving opt-in and default-off. Head lines 107, 116 and 143 enforce that input for Swift build, newly added SwiftPM repository, and Metal cache saves. SwiftPM keys include OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles (47–53), with lane-scoped fallback. This creates additional cached dependency inputs, but the supplied evidence does not establish an adversarial writer accessible to trusted jobs. No supported cache-poisoning finding follows. Git connectivity checking would not authenticate configuration, hooks or refs.

.github/workflows/docs-impact.yml:61–68 adds partial/sparse checkout without changing the visible validation commands. The documentation patches describe branch-restricted saves, credential-free Git caches and separate full-history keys; these descriptions do not prove workflow enforcement or runner-cache isolation. The action's saving contract aligns with the reported ci.yml callers, but those callers cannot be independently verified from this replay.

Relevant contracts are artifact/source integrity and qualification (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054). No replayed change modifies serving authorization, attestation proofs, inference encryption, billing, privileged helpers or the runtime prefix-cache controls in T-041. CI repository caches are distinct from that encrypted inference cache.

Remaining material review: inspect omitted ci.yml source, particularly SAVE_CACHES at head 19, checkout/save blocks at 57–93 and 163–197, action callers at 266/507, and cluster key construction at 916–922. Confirm every new cache producer obeys the trusted-push predicate, checkout removes credentials before Git saves, and restored refs cannot alter build identity/provenance. No concrete regression is established by the available replay; this is not full-PR clearance.
